flags.current: The source describes it exactly this way: changes in the stock price affect the hedge asymmetrically, and the gain or loss on the short stock position tends to exceed the corresponding loss or gain on the convertible bond.
flags.proposed: The source describes the effect as an asymmetry: changes in the stock price affect the hedge asymmetrically. When the stock falls, the gain on the short stock exceeds the loss on the convertible; when it rises, the gain on the convertible exceeds the loss on the short stock.
flags.source_says: PDF p.19 has the same sentence as the JSON. The Schweser-based notes (notes/FRM_Consolidated_Vol2/ch/23_IM_IM8.tex l.163) say it too: 'Whether the stock rises or falls, the gain or loss on the short stock position tends to exceed the corresponding loss or gain on the convertible.'
flags.derivation: Read literally, the quoted sentence says that on a rise the short-stock loss exceeds the convertible gain, so the hedged book loses. That contradicts the row just before it ('In both directions the convex leg outperforms the linear leg') and the bank's own numbers in IR-T2-44: stock +5% gives a convertible gain of 1038.07-1013.75 = +24.32 against a short-stock loss of 11.238*2.077 = -23.34, net +0.98. Stock -5% gives a short-stock gain of +23.34 against a convertible loss of -21.97, net +1.37. So the convertible leg dominates on the upside and the stock leg dominates on the downside. Key (a) is unaffected.
flags.evidence: PDF p.19 Q23 solution paragraph after the table; PDF p.35 S3 Step 3 table (Up 5%: +0.98)

flags.proposed: $$R_{asset} = R_{policy\,mix} + R_{active\,mgt} = \sum_i w_i^B R_i^B + \sum_i (w_i R_i - w_i^B R_i^B)$$
flags.source_says: PDF p.5: 'Rasset = Rpolicy mix + Ractive mgt = Σi wB i R B i + Σi ( wiRi − wBiR B i )', where the policy weights carry superscript B.
flags.derivation: In the Jorion decomposition the policy mix uses the policy (benchmark) weights w_i^B, and active management uses the actual weights w_i. With the B dropped from the weights, the active term reduces to pure within-sleeve benchmark deviations, and the asset-allocation deviation from the policy mix disappears. The solution's own next paragraph relies on that deviation ('the current asset-allocation mix may deviate temporarily from the policy mix').
flags.evidence: PDF p.5 Q5 solution formula; PDF p.4 LO2 reference table
